## Fix ATTACH property parsing to correctly handle binary values

The ICalendar grammar currently misinterprets ATTACH properties that use binary-encoded values (via BASE64 encoding with VALUE=BINARY) as URLs. The goal is to update the attach rule so it properly distinguishes between URI and binary value types, ensuring that binary attachments containing base64-encoded content are parsed correctly. This also requires the grammar to handle the case where binary content may be split across multiple lines with folding whitespace.

    WITH

# Trino grammar for ANTLR4

An ANTLR4 grammar for Trino, formerly known as PrestoSQL.
This grammar is based on the actively maintained [Trino repository](https://github.com/trinodb/trino).

The lexer and parser are referenced from the [offical base antlr file](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/blob/master/core/trino-parser/src/main/antlr4/io/trino/sql/parser/SqlBase.g4).
Changes are made to accommodate various language targets as the official one is being developed for Java only.

The examples are extracted from the [offical test file](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/blob/master/core/trino-parser/src/test/java/io/trino/sql/parser/TestSqlParser.java).

1: 
2: # Grammars-v4 House Rules
3: 
4: ## Ground Rules
5: 
6: * All contributions are welcome ranging from spelling mistakes to new grammars. Grammars-v4 aims to be a welcoming community in which both novice and expert contributors are welcome.  "How do I?" questions are welcomed, and encouraged.
7: * The repository owner [teverett](https://github.com/teverett/), holds final approval on all commits, and changes to the repository
8: * No hate speech, racism, sexism, or ethnocentrism is tolerated. Trolling and personal attacks are not welcome.
9: 
10: ## Contributing
11: 
12: New grammars and bug fixes are welcome.  All changes must pass CI in order to be pulled.  Examples for new grammars are strongly encouraged.  If new features or bug fixes are added to grammars, examples that exercise the feature or fix are also strongly encouraged.
13: 
14: ## Traditions 
15: 
16: * In general, contributors are thanked for every commit
17: * Symbol conflicts are generally resolved by appending an underscore to identifiers. For example "id" becomes "id_"
18: * The formatting style produced by [Antlr4Formatter](https://github.com/antlr/Antlr4Formatter) is the typical code formatting for grammars
19: 
20: ## History of Grammars-V4
21: 
22: The grammars-v4 repository was created `Tue Sep 25 16:45:12 2012 -0700`.  The repository was created as a place to hold grammars for [Antlr4](https://www.antlr.org/).  There is also a [grammars-v3](https://github.com/antlr/grammars-v3) repository here which has the grammars from the legacy [grammars-v3 list](https://www.antlr3.org/grammar/list.html).
23: 
24: In Sept of 2012, the only library of formal grammars was the [grammars-v3 list](https://www.antlr3.org/grammar/list.html), and it really wasn't possible to know if the grammars on that list would pass minimal tests.
25: 
26: In order to ensure that the grammars on the tree worked, to a minimal degree, [antlr4test-maven-plugin](https://github.com/antlr/antlr4test-maven-plugin) was written and Travis CI/CD was set up to ensure that every grammar on the tree passed these tests:
27: 
28: * The grammar is parseable by the current version of Antlr
29: * The generated lexer-parser will parse at least one sample input with the current version of Antlr.
30: 
31: There is no single license for the Antlr4 grammars.  Some of the grammars on the tree were forward-ported from grammrs-v3 and in those cases the original author information was usually included.  Many of the grammars have licensing information in the .g4 file(s).
32: 
33: It has long been the intention of grammars-v4 to provide an ecosystem of grammars for Antlr4 that would enable Antlr4 users to create parsers for the source and target language of thier choice for a wide variety of source languages.  At this time there are a little less than 300-ish source language grammars, and Antlr4 supports many targets including C, Java, C#, Python, JS, Swift and others. 
34: 
35: It is a tradition to thank every contributor to grammars-v4 for the time and effort they put into their pull requests.  There is a "thank-you" for every PR when it is pulled onto the tree.  Additionally grammars-v4 aims to be a welcoming community for all contributors both experienced and novice to contribute to, and to learn from.

import re, sys
from collections import defaultdict

G = open('/data/repo/asm/riscv/riscv.g4').read()

# ---------- split parser rules and lexer rules ----------
# strip block comments (risky with quotes, but our grammar has no quotes in comments except license)
def strip_comments(t):
    t = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', t, flags=re.S)
    t = re.sub(r'//[^\n]*', '', t)
    return t

body = strip_comments(G)
# remove the antlr-format comment lines that start with //  (already removed above)

lines = body.split('\n')
# grammar header
m = re.search(r'grammar\s+(\w+)\s*;', body)
print("grammar name:", m.group(1) if m else "NOT FOUND")

# find rule definitions (leftmost: name colon)
def find_rules(text):
    rules = []
    i = 0
    # find all "NAME :" at line start
    for mm in re.finditer(r'^([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*:\s*(.*)$', text, re.M):
        rules.append((mm.group(1), mm.group(2)))
    return rules

raw_rules = find_rules(body)
names = [n for n,_ in raw_rules]
print("total rule defs:", len(names))

# Determine lexer vs parser: lexer rules start uppercase? ANTLR convention: lexer rules begin uppercase.
parser_rules = [n for n in names if n[0].islower()]
lexer_rules  = [n for n in names if n[0].isupper()]
fragments    = [n for n in lexer_rules if re.search(r'^fragment\s+'+n+r'\b', body, re.M)]
print("parser rules:", len(parser_rules))
print("lexer rules:", len(lexer_rules), "fragments:", len(fragments))
print("parser rule set:", sorted(parser_rules))

# ---------- duplicate literals among lexer rules (case-insensitive) ----------
# extract literals from each lexer rule body (before the semicolon)
def rule_body(name, text):
    mm = re.search(r'^'+re.escape(name)+r'\s*:\s*(.*?);\s*$', text, re.M | re.S)
    return mm.group(1) if mm else None

def literals_in(rtxt):
    return re.findall(r"'((?:\\.|[^'])*)'", rtxt, re.S)

lit_owner = defaultdict(list)
for n in lexer_rules:
    rb = rule_body(n, body)
    if rb is None:
        print("!! no body for", n); continue
    for lit in literals_in(rb):
        key = lit.lower()
        lit_owner[key].append((n, lit))

dups = {k:v for k,v in lit_owner.items() if len(v)>1}
print("\nduplicate literals (case-insensitive):", len(dups))
for k,v in dups.items():
    print("  ", repr(k), v)

# characters in char classes can overlap; check for identical literal rules
# (e.g. two rules both literal-only same string) - ANTLR errors on duplicate string literals.
literal_only = {}
for n in lexer_rules:
    rb = rule_body(n, body)
    if rb and re.fullmatch(r"'(?:\\.|[^'])*'", rb.strip(), re.S):
        lit = re.search(r"'((?:\\.|[^'])*)'", rb, re.S).group(1)
        literal_only.setdefault(lit.lower(), []).append(n)
for k,v in literal_only.items():
    if len(v)>1:
        print("  !! duplicate literal-only rule:", k, v)

# ---------- references in parser rules exist ----------
parser_defs = {n: rule_body(n, body) for n in parser_rules}
all_refs = []
for n, rb in parser_defs.items():
    if rb is None:
        print("!! no body for parser rule", n); continue
    refs = re.findall(r'\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\b', rb)
    all_refs += refs
    refs_r = re.findall(r'\b([a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\b', rb)
    for r in refs_r:
        if r not in parser_rules and r not in ('e','i','n','x','w','d','s','a','p','m','r','t','f','l','g','o','b','h','v','u'):  # ignore short identifier chars inside rules? they are actual rule refs
            pass
undefined_tokens = set(all_refs) - set(lexer_rules) - {'EOF'}
print("\nparser refs to undefined tokens:", sorted(undefined_tokens))

# token rules not referenced anywhere (may be fine if hidden/skip)
used = set(all_refs)
unused_tokens = [n for n in lexer_rules if n not in used and n not in fragments]
print("lexer rules never referenced in parser:", unused_tokens)

# lexer fragments referenced
for f in fragments:
    if not re.search(r'\b'+f+r'\b', body):
        print("!! fragment never used:", f)

# ---------- balanced parens/brackets in the whole grammar ----------
for ch_open, ch_close in [('(',')'),('{','}'),('[',']')]:
    if body.count(ch_open) != body.count(ch_close):
        print(f"!! unbalanced {ch_open}{ch_close}: {body.count(ch_open)} vs {body.count(ch_close)}")
print("\nstructural checks done")

import re, sys

# ================= Lexer (models ANTLR4 longest-match, order tie-break) =================

def lit(s):
    return re.escape(s).replace('\\ ',' ')

def L(name, pat):
    return (name, pat)

# order must match the order lexer rules appear in riscv.g4
TOKEN_RULES = [
    L('ADD', lit('add')), L('SUB', lit('sub')), L('SLL', lit('sll')), L('SLT', lit('slt')),
    L('SLTU', lit('sltu')), L('XOR', lit('xor')), L('SRL', lit('srl')), L('SRA', lit('sra')),
    L('OR', lit('or')), L('AND', lit('and')),
    L('ADDI', lit('addi')), L('SLTI', lit('slti')), L('SLTIU', lit('sltiu')), L('XORI', lit('xori')),
    L('ORI', lit('ori')), L('ANDI', lit('andi')), L('SLLI', lit('slli')), L('SRLI', lit('srli')),
    L('SRAI', lit('srai')),
    L('LB', lit('lb')), L('LH', lit('lh')), L('LW', lit('lw')), L('LD', lit('ld')),
    L('LBU', lit('lbu')), L('LHU', lit('lhu')), L('LWU', lit('lwu')),
    L('SB', lit('sb')), L('SH', lit('sh')), L('SW', lit('sw')), L('SD', lit('sd')),
    L('BEQ', lit('beq')), L('BNE', lit('bne')), L('BLT', lit('blt')), L('BGE', lit('bge')),
    L('BLTU', lit('bltu')), L('BGEU', lit('bgeu')),
    L('LUI', lit('lui')), L('AUIPC', lit('auipc')), L('JAL', lit('jal')), L('JALR', lit('jalr')),
    L('FENCE', lit('fence')), L('FENCE_I', lit('fence.i')), L('FENCE_TSO', lit('fence.tso')),
    L('ECALL', lit('ecall')), L('EBREAK', lit('ebreak')),
    L('MUL', lit('mul')), L('MULH', lit('mulh')), L('MULHSU', lit('mulhsu')), L('MULHU', lit('mulhu')),
    L('DIV', lit('div')), L('DIVU', lit('divu')), L('REM', lit('rem')), L('REMU', lit('remu')),
    L('MULW', lit('mulw')), L('DIVW', lit('divw')), L('DIVUW', lit('divuw')), L('REMW', lit('remw')),
    L('REMUW', lit('remuw')),
    L('LR', r'lr\.[wd](\.(aq|rl|aqrl))?'),
    L('SC', r'sc\.[wd](\.(aq|rl|aqrl))?'),
    L('AMO', r'amo(swap|add|xor|and|or|min|max|minu|maxu)\.[wd](\.(aq|rl|aqrl))?'),
    L('FLW', lit('flw')), L('FSW', lit('fsw')), L('FLD', lit('fld')), L('FSD', lit('fsd')),
    L('FADD', r'fadd\.[sd]'), L('FSUB', r'fsub\.[sd]'), L('FMUL', r'fmul\.[sd]'), L('FDIV', r'fdiv\.[sd]'),
    L('FSQRT', r'fsqrt\.[sd]'), L('FSGNJ', r'fsgnj(n|x)?\.[sd]'), L('FMIN', r'fmin\.[sd]'),
    L('FMAX', r'fmax\.[sd]'), L('FEQ', r'feq\.[sd]'), L('FLT', r'flt\.[sd]'), L('FLE', r'fle\.[sd]'),
    L('FCLASS', r'fclass\.[sd]'),
    L('FMADD', r'fmadd\.[sd]'), L('FMSUB', r'fmsub\.[sd]'), L('FNMSUB', r'fnmsub\.[sd]'), L('FNMADD', r'fnmadd\.[sd]'),
    L('FMV', r'fmv\.(x\.w|w\.x|x\.d|d\.x)'),
    L('FCVT', r'fcvt\.(w\.s|wu\.s|l\.s|lu\.s|s\.w|s\.wu|s\.l|s\.lu|w\.d|wu\.d|l\.d|lu\.d|d\.w|d\.wu|d\.l|d\.lu|s\.d|d\.s)'),
    L('C_ADDI4SPN', lit('c.addi4spn')), L('C_LW', lit('c.lw')), L('C_LD', lit('c.ld')),
    L('C_SW', lit('c.sw')), L('C_SD', lit('c.sd')), L('C_FLW', lit('c.flw')), L('C_FLD', lit('c.fld')),
    L('C_FSW', lit('c.fsw')), L('C_FSD', lit('c.fsd')), L('C_ADDI', lit('c.addi')), L('C_LI', lit('c.li')),
    L('C_ADDI16SP', lit('c.addi16sp')), L('C_LUI', lit('c.lui')), L('C_SRLI', lit('c.srli')),
    L('C_SRAI', lit('c.srai')), L('C_ANDI', lit('c.andi')), L('C_SUB', lit('c.sub')), L('C_XOR', lit('c.xor')),
    L('C_OR', lit('c.or')), L('C_AND', lit('c.and')), L('C_SUBW', lit('c.subw')), L('C_ADDW', lit('c.addw')),
    L('C_J', lit('c.j')), L('C_JAL', lit('c.jal')), L('C_BEQZ', lit('c.beqz')), L('C_BNEZ', lit('c.bnez')),
    L('C_SLLI', lit('c.slli')), L('C_LWSP', lit('c.lwsp')), L('C_LDSP', lit('c.ldsp')), L('C_JR', lit('c.jr')),
    L('C_MV', lit('c.mv')), L('C_EBREAK', lit('c.ebreak')), L('C_JALR', lit('c.jalr')), L('C_ADD', lit('c.add')),
    L('C_SWSP', lit('c.swsp')), L('C_SDSP', lit('c.sdsp')), L('C_FLWSP', lit('c.flwsp')),
    L('C_FLDSP', lit('c.fldsp')), L('C_FSWSP', lit('c.fswsp')), L('C_FSDSP', lit('c.fsdsp')),
    L('C_NOP', lit('c.nop')),
]
# registers
reg_names = ([f'X{i}' for i in range(32)] + ['ZERO','RA','SP','GP','TP','FP'] +
             [f'S{i}' for i in range(12)] + [f'T{i}' for i in range(7)] + [f'A{i}' for i in range(8)] +
             [f'F{i}' for i in range(32)] + [f'FT{i}' for i in range(12)] +
             [f'FS{i}' for i in range(12)] + [f'FA{i}' for i in range(8)])
for n in reg_names:
    TOKEN_RULES.append(L(n, lit(n.lower())))
TOKEN_RULES += [
    L('DOT_IDENTIFIER', r'\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*'),
    L('SYMBOL', r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*|\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*'),
    L('STRING_LITERAL', r'"(\\[\s\S]|[^"\\\r\n])*"'),
    L('COMMA', lit(',')), L('COLON', lit(':')), L('LPAREN', lit('(')), L('RPAREN', lit(')')),
    L('PLUS', lit('+')), L('MINUS', lit('-')), L('STAR', lit('*')), L('SLASH', lit('/')),
    L('AT', lit('@')), L('PERCENT', lit('%')), L('DOT', lit('.')),
    L('NUMBER', r'0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]([0-9a-fA-F_])*(\.([0-9a-fA-F_]+))?([pP][+-]?\d+)?|'
               r'0[bB][01]([01_])*|'
               r'\d+(\.\d*)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?|'
               r'\.\d+([eE][+-]?\d+)?'),
    L('EOL', r'[\r\n]+'),
    L('COMMENT_SKIP', r'#[^\r\n]*'),
    L('WS_SKIP', r'[ \t]+'),
]

compiled = [(n, re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE | re.S)) for n, p in TOKEN_RULES]

def lex(text):
    toks = []
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(text):
        best = None
        for n, rx in compiled:
            m = rx.match(text, pos)
            if m:
                ln = m.end()-m.start()
                if best is None or ln > best[1]:
                    best = (n, ln, m)
        assert best, f"no token at pos {pos}: {text[pos:pos+20]!r}"
        n, ln, m = best
        val = m.group(0)
        pos = m.end()
        if n.endswith('_SKIP'):
            continue
        toks.append((n, val))
    toks.append(('EOF',''))
    return toks

OPCODE_SET = set(n for n,_ in TOKEN_RULES if n not in set(reg_names) and n not in
    ['DOT_IDENTIFIER','SYMBOL','STRING_LITERAL','COMMA','COLON','LPAREN','RPAREN','PLUS','MINUS','STAR','SLASH','AT','PERCENT','DOT','NUMBER','EOL','COMMENT_SKIP','WS_SKIP'])
REG_SECOND = set(reg_names)

# ================= Parser (recursive descent mirroring the grammar decisions) =================

class P:
    def __init__(self, toks): self.t = toks; self.i = 0
    def cur(self): return self.t[self.i]
    def nxt(self, k=1): 
        j = min(self.i+k, len(self.t)-1); return self.t[j]
    def aix(self, *types): return self.cur()[0] in types
    def eat(self):
        n = self.cur()[0]; self.i += 1; return n
    def expect(self, *types):
        n = self.cur()
        assert n[0] in types, f"expected {types} got {n}"
        self.i += 1; return n

    def at_name(self):
        return self.aix('SYMBOL','DOT_IDENTIFIER','NUMBER')
    def at_opcode(self):
        return self.cur()[0] in OPCODE_SET
    def at_reg(self):
        return self.cur()[0] in REG_SECOND

    def prog(self):
        while self.cur()[0] != 'EOF':
            self.line()
        # optionally a trailing label?statement?EOF handled by line()
    def line(self):
        # label?
        if self.at_name() and self.nxt()[0] == 'COLON':
            name = self.eat(); self.expect('COLON')
        # statement?
        if self.aix('EOF','EOL'):
            pass
        elif self.at_opcode():
            self.instruction()
        elif self.cur()[0] == 'DOT_IDENTIFIER':
            self.directive()
        # line terminator
        n = self.cur()
        if n[0] == 'EOL':
            while self.cur()[0] == 'EOL':
                self.eat()
        else:
            assert n[0] == 'EOF', f"expected EOL/EOF got {n}"
    def instruction(self):
        self.expect(*OPCODE_SET)
        if not self.aix('EOL','EOF','COMMA','COLON') and self.cur()[0] != 'LPAREN':
            self.operandList()
    def directive(self):
        self.expect('DOT_IDENTIFIER')
        if not self.aix('EOL','EOF','COMMA'):
            self.operandList()
    def operandList(self):
        self.operand()
        while self.aix('COMMA'):
            self.eat(); self.operand()
    def operand(self):
        if self.at_reg():
            self.eat(); return
        if self.aix('STRING_LITERAL'):
            self.eat(); return
        if self.aix('LPAREN'):
            self.eat(); self.expect(*REG_SECOND); self.expect('RPAREN'); return
        # expression optionally followed by (register)
        self.expression()
        if self.aix('LPAREN'):
            self.eat(); self.expect(*REG_SECOND); self.expect('RPAREN')
    def expression(self):
        self.term()
        while self.aix('PLUS','MINUS'):
            self.eat(); self.term()
    def term(self):
        self.factor()
        while self.aix('STAR','SLASH'):
            self.eat(); self.factor()
    def factor(self):
        if self.aix('PLUS','MINUS'):
            self.eat()
        self.primary()
    def primary(self):
        n = self.cur()[0]
        if n in ('NUMBER','SYMBOL','DOT_IDENTIFIER','DOT'):
            self.eat()
        elif n == 'AT':
            self.eat(); self.expect('SYMBOL')
        elif n == 'PERCENT':
            self.eat(); self.expect('SYMBOL'); self.expect('LPAREN'); self.expression(); self.expect('RPAREN')
        else:
            assert False, f"bad primary {self.cur()}"

def parse_file(path):
    text = open(path).read()
    toks = lex(text)
    # collapse consecutive EOL into one? keep: line() loops over EOLs
    p = P(toks)
    try:
        p.prog()
        assert p.cur()[0] == 'EOF'
        return True, []
    except AssertionError as e:
        # locate offending line
        lineno = text[:sum(len(v)+0 for _,(_,v) in toks[:min(p.i,len(toks)-1)])].count('\n') if p.i is not None else -1
        return False, [f"parse fail near token #{p.i} {p.cur()!r}, msg={e}"]

ok = True
for f in ['/data/repo/asm/riscv/examples/arithmetic.S',
          '/data/repo/asm/riscv/examples/floatingpoint.S']:
    r, errs = parse_file(f)
    print(f, "PARSE-OK" if r else "PARSE-FAIL", errs[:5])
    ok = ok and r

# Also lex-all sanity: ensure every visible token in examples is recognized (done inside lex)

sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

An ANTLR4 grammar for [RISC-V](https://riscv.org/) 64-bit assembly files
produced by the GNU assembler (`riscv64-linux-gnu-as`).

The grammar covers the unprivileged G base integer ISA (RV64I) together with
the standard queried extensions:

* RV64M multiply/divide
* RV64A atomics (`lr`, `sc`, `amoswap`, `amoadd`, ...)
* RV64F single-precision floating-point
* RV64D double-precision floating-point
* RV64C compressed instructions

Compiler pseudo-instructions (for example `li`, `la`, `mv`, `ret`, `call`,
`tail`, `j`, `nop`) are deliberately not part of the grammar.

610: valueStmt

613:     | NEW WS valueStmt                                                         # vsNew

615:     | ADDRESSOF WS valueStmt                                                   # vsAddressOf
616:     | implicitCallStmt_InStmt WS? ASSIGN WS? valueStmt                         # vsAssign
617:     | valueStmt WS? POW WS? valueStmt                                          # vsPow
618:     | (PLUS | MINUS) WS? valueStmt                                             # vsPlusMinus
619:     | valueStmt WS? (MULT | DIV) WS? valueStmt                                 # vsMultDiv
620:     | valueStmt WS? (IDIV) WS? valueStmt                                       # vsIDiv
621:     | valueStmt WS? MOD WS? valueStmt                                          # vsMod
622:     | valueStmt WS? (PLUS | MINUS) WS? valueStmt                               # vsAddSub
623:     | valueStmt WS? AMPERSAND WS? valueStmt                                    # vsAmp
624:     | valueStmt WS? (EQ | NEQ | LT | GT | LEQ | GEQ | LIKE | IS) WS? valueStmt # vsComp
625:     | NOT (WS valueStmt | LPAREN WS? valueStmt WS? RPAREN)                     # vsNot
626:     | valueStmt WS? AND WS? valueStmt                                          # vsAnd
627:     | valueStmt WS? OR WS? valueStmt                                           # vsOr
628:     | valueStmt WS? XOR WS? valueStmt                                          # vsXor
629:     | valueStmt WS? EQV WS? valueStmt                                          # vsEqv
630:     | valueStmt WS? IMP WS? valueStmt                                          # vsImp

681:     )?

695: iCS_B_MemberProcedureCall
696:     : implicitCallStmt_InStmt? DOT ambiguousIdentifier typeHint? (WS argsCall)? dictionaryCallStmt?

699: // iCS_S_MembersCall first, so that member calls are not resolved as separate iCS_S_VariableOrProcedureCalls
700: implicitCallStmt_InStmt

702:     | iCS_S_VariableOrProcedureCall
703:     | iCS_S_ProcedureOrArrayCall
704:     | iCS_S_DictionaryCall

707: iCS_S_VariableOrProcedureCall

713:         LPAREN WS? (argsCall WS?)? RPAREN
714:     )+ dictionaryCallStmt?

716:

718:     : ambiguousIdentifier typeHint? WS? LPAREN WS? (argsCall WS?)? RPAREN

49:     }

51:     protected boolean notOpenBraceAndNotFunction() {
52:         int nextTokenType = _input.LT(1).getType();
53:         return nextTokenType != JavaScriptParser.OpenBrace && nextTokenType != JavaScriptParser.Function_;
54:     }

56:     protected boolean closeBrace() {
57:         return _input.LT(1).getType() == JavaScriptParser.CloseBrace;
58:     }

61:      * Returns {@code true} iff on the current index of the parser's
62:      * token stream a token of the given {@code type} exists on the
63:      * {@code HIDDEN} channel.
64:      *
65:      * @param type
66:      *         the type of the token on the {@code HIDDEN} channel
67:      *         to check.
68:      *
69:      * @return {@code true} iff on the current index of the parser's
70:      * token stream a token of the given {@code type} exists on the
71:      * {@code HIDDEN} channel.
72:      */
73:     private boolean here(final int type) {
74: 
75:         // Get the token ahead of the current index.
76:         int possibleIndexEosToken = this.getCurrentToken().getTokenIndex() - 1;
77:         Token ahead = _input.get(possibleIndexEosToken);
78: 
79:         // Check if the token resides on the HIDDEN channel and if it's of the
80:         // provided type.
81:         return (ahead.getChannel() == Lexer.HIDDEN) && (ahead.getType() == type);

92:      * either is a line terminator, or is a multi line comment that
93:      * contains a line terminator.

95:     protected boolean lineTerminatorAhead() {
96: 
97:         // Get the token ahead of the current index.
98:         int possibleIndexEosToken = this.getCurrentToken().getTokenIndex() - 1;
99:         Token ahead = _input.get(possibleIndexEosToken);
100: 
101:         if (ahead.getChannel() != Lexer.HIDDEN) {
102:             // We're only interested in tokens on the HIDDEN channel.
103:             return false;
104:         }
105: 
106:         if (ahead.getType() == JavaScriptParser.LineTerminator) {
107:             // There is definitely a line terminator ahead.
108:             return true;
109:         }
110: 
111:         if (ahead.getType() == JavaScriptParser.WhiteSpaces) {
112:             // Get the token ahead of the current whitespaces.
113:             possibleIndexEosToken = this.getCurrentToken().getTokenIndex() - 2;
114:             ahead = _input.get(possibleIndexEosToken);

119:         int type = ahead.getType();
120: 
121:         // Check if the token is, or contains a line terminator.
122:         return (type == JavaScriptParser.MultiLineComment && (text.contains("\r") || text.contains("\n"))) ||
